FIGlet - Frank, Ian & Glenn's Letters
======================================

FIGlet is a program that creates large characters out of ordinary screen characters.

Example:

 _ _ _          _   _     _       
| (_) | _____  | |_| |__ (_)___   
| | | |/ / _ \ | __| '_ \| / __|  
| | |   <  __/ | |_| | | | \__ \_ 
|_|_|_|\_\___|  \__|_| |_|_|___(_)

FIGlet can create characters in many different styles and can kern and "smush" 
these characters together in various ways. FIGlet output is generally reminiscent 
of the sort of "signatures" many people like to put at the end of e-mail and 
UseNet messages.

Official FIGlet web page: http://www.figlet.org/
Contact: info@figlet.org


Usage
-----

Basic usage:
    figlet [options] [message]

If no message is provided, FIGlet reads from standard input.

Examples:
    figlet Hello, world!
    echo "Hello, world!" | figlet
    figlet -f banner "Hello"


Command Line Options
--------------------

Font and Layout:
    -f <fontfile>       Use the specified font
    -d <fontdir>        Specify directory for fonts
    -c                  Center the output
    -l                  Left-align the output (default)
    -r                  Right-align the output
    -k                  Use kerning (reduce spacing between characters)
    -W                  Full-width mode (no character smushing)
    -o                  Overlap mode
    -m <mode>           Specify layout mode

Text Direction:
    -L                  Left-to-right text (default)
    -R                  Right-to-left text

Output Control:
    -w <width>          Specify output width
    -t                  Use terminal width for output
    -p                  Paragraph mode (for multi-line input)

Control Files:
    -C <controlfile>    Use specified control file
    -N                  Clear control file list

Information:

                        -I 1: version
                        -I 2: default font directory
                        -I 3: default font
                        -I 4: output width

Other:

Available Fonts
---------------

FIGlet comes with numerous fonts stored in the fonts/ directory.
Font files have the extension .flf (FIGlet font) or .flc (FIGlet control file).

    - big         - Large letters

    - digital     - Digital display style
    - ivrit       - Hebrew (right-to-left)

    - shadow      - Letters with shadow
    - slant       - Slanted letters
    - small       - Small letters
    - standard    - Standard font (default)
    - term        - Terminal-style letters

And many more fonts and control files for various character sets and languages.
